title: Application Security Engineer
description:
About Opal Security:

At Opal, we’re building modern identity governance for the AI era—intelligent access management that empowers enterprises to move fast while staying secure. Our mission is to bring clarity, control, and confidence to complex enterprise environments, helping teams govern access without slowing down innovation.

The Role:

Most security engineers spend their careers bolting locks onto doors that were already built. This is not that job.

We're hiring an Application Security Engineer to own security across Opal's product and platform — and yes, own means what it sounds like. You'd be our dedicated security engineer, embedded directly with engineering, writing production code in Go and TypeScript, and building security into the product while it's still being designed. You’ll work closely with a team of engineers that genuinely care about getting this right, and a product that happens to be one of the most security-critical tools in enterprise software.

Oh, and one more thing: Opal is a security company. We sell access control to organizations that take security seriously. That means your work isn't a cost center — it's core to what we do.

This role lives on the Platform team and partners closely with Infrastructure Engineering on cloud security. It is explicitly scoped to application and product security — enterprise IT, compliance, and vendor risk management are handled separately.

What You’ll Do:

Secure Development Lifecycle -

  • Own the secure SDLC end-to-end: threat modeling, design reviews, code reviews — you set the bar

  • Run and coordinate app pentests (internal and external) and drive findings to closure

  • Build and own SAST/DAST/SCA tooling wired into CI/CD so security ships with the code

  • Triage and remediate vulnerabilities from every angle — bug bounty, internal scans, the works

Software Security Engineering -

  • Build and maintain the security-critical stuff: encryption services, authz enforcement, authn flows

  • Own the Auth0 ↔ Opal integration — tokens, sessions, MFA, SSO (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0)

  • Ship production Go and TypeScript to harden APIs, enforce least-privilege, and close vuln classes for good

  • Create shared libraries that make the secure path the easy path for every product engineer

Incident Response & Cloud Security -

  • Be first on the scene for security incidents: investigate, contain, find the root cause, fix it

  • Partner with Infra on cloud hardening — AWS IAM, EKS, KMS, network segmentation

  • Level up detection and response by writing detection rules and improving logging and alerting

Security Culture -

  • Mentor engineers on secure coding, common vuln patterns, and security architecture — you make the org smarter

  • Help set the security roadmap by grounding it in real product risk

  • Be the security teammate engineers want to work with — a collaborator, not a bottleneck

You Might Be a Fit If You:

  • Have 4+ years in application security or software security engineering

  • Actually write production code — findings reports are the floor, not the ceiling

  • Know auth cold: OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, session management, token lifecycle

  • Are comfortable in AWS and containerized environments (Kubernetes, Docker)

  • Bonus points for familiarity with our stack: Go, TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL, Redis, GraphQL

  • Have led complex, cross-functional security initiatives from kickoff to completion

  • Have run or participated in external pentests and seen findings through remediation

  • Thrive on ownership and ambiguity — you'd rather write the playbook than wait for one

title: Postdoctoral Research Scientist, Ocean CDR Atlas
description:
About [C]Worthy

[C]Worthy is a non-profit research organization transforming research-grade oceanographic models into open, reproducible, and auditable decision-support tools for ocean-based carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Ocean CDR technologies, leveraging the ocean’s vast natural capacity to absorb and store atmospheric carbon dioxide, have the potential to make significant contributions to climate change mitigation alongside deep emissions reductions, as the world works to meet global climate targets. However, because the ocean is a dynamic, open system, measuring how much carbon a given CDR intervention actually removes presents a major scientific challenge. This is why robust Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) is essential: transparent, science-backed MRV builds the trust needed for governments, communities, and carbon markets to research and scale safe, effective ocean-based solutions to climate change.

At [C]Worthy, we are building C-Star, an open-source modeling platform that systematizes regional biogeochemical ocean modeling through automated, reproducible workflows, functioning as a one-stop-shop to create input and forcing data, model configurations, model execution, postpost-processing, and analysis. We use this software for a range of applications within CDR research and MRV applications, and work with external partners to establish a broad user-base of our software within both academia and industry.

By establishing shared, open-source infrastructure, validated model domains, and reusable workflows, we dramatically lower the barrier to entry for new ocean modeling projects and ensure scientific innovations benefit the broader community. Ultimately, we aim to democratize access to advanced ocean modeling tools—empowering researchers, policymakers, and local communities to actively shape ocean governance and marine resource management.

[C]Worthy is headquartered in Boulder, Colorado.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Postdoctoral Research Scientist to work with our team on the development of a high-resolution Ocean CDR Atlas dataset. The goal of the Atlas is to simulate ocean CDR interventions, such as ocean enhanced alkalinity (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR) across a range of locations spanning the continental west coast of the United States of America.

This is a unique postdoctoral position, which sits at the intersection of academia and industry, offering multiple learning and career-advancing opportunities at once:

  • Answer central scientific questions at the frontier of ocean carbon capture research
  • Use cutting edge open-source ocean models and ocean modelling tools paving the way for others to follow your steps
  • Design and develop data visualization tools specific to large geospatial datasets
  • Interact with both academic and industry researchers and practitioners of ocean carbon capture
  • Gain skills in scientific software development and contribute to collaborative open-source software packages

Key Responsibilities

The postdoctoral scientist will receive training in how to configure and validate a mesoscale-resolving domain spanning the Pacific ocean using reproducible [C]Worthy software tools and workflows, and will subsequently design and analyze production grade Atlas simulations. These simulations will enable the postdoctoral scientist to conduct research identifying which release locations and intervention technologies have the potential to achieve the highest carbon uptake efficiency, and to what extent release depth, seasonality and inter-annual variability matters for short term and long term ocean carbon uptake. The Atlas simulations will be performed with the ROMS regional ocean model within C-Star.

The next step is to work with a broader team to design and implement a public data hosting strategy, including data visualization, and to release the Atlas as a public, documented dataset enabling MRV calculations. Finally, the postdoc may work with external collaborators to establish nested submesoscale domains within the broader Pacific domain to research mixed-layer exchange dynamics associated at 1–10 km scales within select CDR intervention locations.

The postdoctoral scientist is expected to produce one or more peer-reviewed manuscripts describing the Atlas methodology and main results, as well as actively engage the data user community—such as CDR deployment operators, MRV practitioners, and academic collaborators—through direct outreach, workshops and conferences.

Required Qualifications

The position is based in Boulder, Colorado (preferred), although hybrid and remote applications will be considered.

  • Ph.D. in oceanography or a closely related field
  • Experience configuring, running, and evaluating ocean model simulations (ROMS, Oceananigans, MITgcm, CESM, or similar)
  • Background in ocean biogeochemistry, including carbonate chemistry
  • Proficiency in gridded dataset analysis using python-packages such as xarray, dask, and numpy
  • Ability to work with large geospatial datasets, and familiarity with file formats such as netcdf and zarr
  • Experience with high-performance computing (HPC) environments
  • Strong written and oral communication skills; ability to collaborate in a small, fast-moving research team

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience configuring and running coupled ocean physics and biogeochemistry model simulations
  • Previous research on the topic of ocean carbon capture
  • Previous experience in open-source scientific software development
This position is full-time, fixed-term (1 year, with possibility of renewal). We expect this role to start as soon as possible.

  • Own program financial performance with Finance, including budgets, actual costs, resource forecasts, estimates at completion, and margin risks. Develop recovery plans when performance deviates.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for program execution. Lead customer reviews, communicate progress and risks candidly, and drive resolution of delivery issues.

  • Control scope and changes with Contracts and Finance. Assess cost, schedule, resource, and technical impacts and obtain required approvals before changing commitments.

  • Coordinate deployment readiness with Operations, including staffing, training, aircraft and equipment availability, subcontractor support, logistics, and sustainment requirements.

  • Manage supplier and subcontractor deliverables with functional owners, tracking dependencies, quality, schedule, and corrective actions that affect customer commitments.

  • Maintain program risks, issues, decisions, and action plans. Escalate material concerns early with clear options, recommendations, and resource tradeoffs for leadership.

  • Track contractual reporting, customer acceptance, and billing milestones. Coordinate applicable security, export, quality, and operational requirements with accountable specialists.

  • Build practical program management processes and capture lessons learned. Coordinate handoffs to Client Success and support through the warranty period.

Required qualifications

  • Eight or more years of relevant program or project management experience, including at least three years leading complex technical programs across multiple functions.

  • Demonstrated delivery of aerospace, defense, unmanned systems, robotics, or comparable hardware and software programs from planning through customer acceptance.

  • Experience managing program budgets, forecasts, integrated schedules, contractual deliverables, risks, and changes; able to connect execution decisions to financial outcomes.

  • Ability to lead through influence, resolve competing priorities, and secure commitments from functional teams in a growing organization.

  • Strong customer-facing communication and executive briefing skills, including the ability to explain technical tradeoffs and escalate issues with actionable recommendations.

  • Working knowledge of engineering development, systems integration, verification and validation, manufacturing, and field operations.

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, program management, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional or military experience.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with unmanned aircraft, autonomy, intelligence and surveillance systems, payload integration, or airborne communications.

  • Experience supporting U.S. government or international defense customers, including product deliveries and contractor-operated services.

  • Familiarity with government contracting, subcontract management, and applicable export or security requirements.

  • PMP certification or equivalent training; experience introducing practical program controls and reporting in a scaling company.

What success looks like

  • Customer commitments are met against approved scope, schedule, cost, and acceptance criteria.

  • Leadership receives accurate forecasts, timely risk escalation, and clear decisions needed to keep programs on track.

  • Engineering, Production, and Operations work from coordinated plans with realistic resource requirements and accountable owners.

description:

title: Additive Technician
description:
At Stoke, we believe a thriving space economy will enable a vibrant, sustainable, and equitable future here on Earth. That is why we’re building Nova, our fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Designed for daily flight, Nova tackles the core challenges of space transportation by reducing cost, increasing availability, and improving reliability. By radically lowering launch costs and increasing flight cadence, we’re helping create a truly scalable space industry.

Our team is mission-driven, collaborative, and empowered to take ownership of their work. If you want to work alongside some of the most dedicated and talented people on Earth, we’d love to have you join us.

Fully reusable launch vehicles are the key to seamlessly connecting Earth and space. We are seeking a full-time Additive Manufacturing (AM) Technician to join our dynamic team. This role is focused on shop floor tasks centered around metallic additive manufacturing technologies. With technical certifications or equivalent work experience and knowledge, the successful candidate will be instrumental in advancing our in-house production capabilities, ensuring regular production of complex aerospace components, and contributing to our mission. You must be ready to stay focused, move fast, self-direct, and learn on the fly.

Responsibilities

  • Take extreme ownership for shop floor operation of a variety of additive machines to deliver hardware with a focus on flexibility and scrappiness needed to accomplish the goal.
  • Hands-on machine operation skills. The candidate should be comfortable operating high value equipment and computer-controlled tools.
  • The candidate will be comfortable delivering results in the face of adversity. When necessary, take action to find creative solutions and collaborate with experts/leaders.
  • Embrace a fast-paced startup environment, staying focused, self-directed, and eager to learn and adapt on the fly.
  • Knowledge and responsibility for mechanical systems necessary to support AM operations including gas and fluid plumbing, shop floor equipment.
  • Ability to engage in manual support removal using air tools, part de-powdering in Solukon, and EDM operation for cutting parts off build plates.
  • Ownership of shop floor cleanliness and organization. The candidate must be able to learn from doing and work towards continuous process improvement by providing feedback and taking ownership of 5S activities.
  • Maintenance of equipment and supporting tools relevant to the manufacturing process.
  • Ability to work safely while manipulating heavy objects and handling metal powders.
  • The candidate will have strong knowledge of hand and power tools, how to use them to accomplish a given task.
  • Digital work order inputs/outputs, ability to follow computer-based directions and provide feedback to engineering staff for continuous improvement of process documentation.

Qualifications

  • No degree requirements if applicant has relevant background work experience necessary to be successful in the role. Examples of relevant experience include working in the construction trades, CNC machining, aerospace assembly technician, or automotive mechanic roles.
  • 1+ years of experience as metal additive manufacturing technician is preferred. 3+ years of total job experience in a relatable field is required.
  • Comfortable with hands-on machine operation of high value and high consequence equipment.
  • Highly organized with the ability to work flexible hours, including second shift and weekends, as needed.
  • Proficient communication skills, willingness to work and collaborate with a team to accomplish goals.
  • Knowledge of general fabrication methods including CNC milling, turning, EDM, welding, bending, etc.
  • Self-starter mindset, maintain focus on the goal and work towards it when input from process experts and leaders is stretched thin.
  • Work with high intensity, maintain status tracking, and project execution ownership in an ambitious environment.
  • Willing to work on site in Kent, WA

Benefits

  • Equity – We know that our employees are the reason we succeed. To give everyone a stake in our future, we are pleased to offer equity in the form of stock options to all regular, full-time employees.
  • Comprehensive benefits program including subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Company-paid life and disability insurance
  • 401(k) plan with employer match
  • 4 weeks’ Paid Time Off
  • Holidays – 10 days (including an end-of-year closure)
  • Paid Family/Parental Leave
  • On-site gym or monthly wellness stipend (depending on location)
  • Dog friendly offices!

Compensation

Target Levels:

  • Level 1 Range: $26.25 - $38.52
  • Level 2 Range: $32.11 - $48.16

Our job posts are intentionally written to attract a wide variety of experience levels, and we make decisions about the right fit on a per-candidate basis.

Your actual level and base salary will be decided based on your specific experience and skill level.

The ED tech/ Registrar plays a critical role in facilitating smooth operations within the emergency department by ensuring timely and accurate registration, assisting with patient needs, and supporting the healthcare team.   1. Provides patient care in a non-judgmental, non-discriminatory manner that considers cultural diversity and age appropriateness so that autonomy, rights, and dignity are preserved.

title: Staff Software Engineer, RestX
description:
About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.

Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.

Our vision

We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.

But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.

Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.

In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.

Our traction

Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an website.

More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.

Our team

Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.

We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.

Where we work

Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!

Why we're looking for you

Today, restaurant owners spend huge amounts of time reacting to operational problems: managing incoming orders, handling kitchen bottlenecks, coordinating delivery, updating menus, and responding to customer issues under constant time pressure.

RestX is building the autonomous operating system for restaurants. We are building systems that detect issues using signals across fragmented systems, automate decisions at scale, and help restaurants run with minimal manual intervention, helping owners focus on their passion: making great food and delighting their customers.

This team owns ordering, fulfillment, menu syncs, POS integrations, kitchen workflows, and operational automations – systems directly in the critical path for restaurant revenue and guest experience.

We're looking for a Staff Backend Engineer, who cares deeply about scale and reliability, while building compelling product experiences and has the range to own it end-to-end. You'll build mission-critical software systems that directly impact restaurant revenue and reputation.

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States and Canada.

Our Tech Stack

  • Frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript

  • Mobile: React Native

  • Backend: Node.js, TypeScript

  • Databases: MongoDB, PostgreSQL

  • TypeScript everywhere

The impact you'll have

  • Build autonomous restaurant operations software and innovate new interaction models between operators and software

  • Work on mission-critical systems that directly impact guest experience with our product, restaurant revenue and reputation, and operate as a leader in reliability and scale

  • Build systems in a domain with rich real-time data loops with immediate customer feedback, and have a direct impact on Owner’s revenue trajectory by greatly reducing support tickets and churn

  • Demonstrate extreme ownership across workflows spanning ordering, kitchens, delivery, and fulfillment

What we're looking for

  • 7+ years, with meaningful time building end-to-end systems and product experiences

  • Strong experience building high-throughput systems with a focus on reliability and scalability

  • Experience with our backend stack (Node.js, MongoDB, PostgreSQL)

  • Experience building workflow orchestration, automation systems, or AI agents

  • High degree of cross-functional collaboration — past colleagues in product, design, and business would speak highly of you

  • Strong sense of ownership and drive, excellent communication, and a proactive approach to identifying and solving problems

Compensation and benefits

  • The estimated starting base salary range for this role is $220K-240K depending on level, location and experience, plus a generous pre-IPO equity package

  • Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, work from anywhere (remote-first workplace), unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!

Notice - Employment Scams

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.

We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

title: (Senior) Embedded Software Engineer
description:
Alif established its first European R&D site to Oulu to be a significant center of expertise and employ teams of Software and Digital IC Design experts, to complement the staff in the US and India. We are headquartered in the US, and our office in the Oulu Technology Park employs about 35 employees.

Our local team consists of very experienced experts as well as younger talents ready to take on new challenges in their careers. Our days here often consist of solving very high-level technical challenges and creating new technology, and we can offer you growth opportunities that are unique and rewarding. We have an open, supportive, and relaxed culture. We enjoy coming to the office and collaborating with one another.

As our Finnish site grows, we are looking for a (Senior) Embedded Software Engineer to our Wireless Connectivity Team, working on 15.4, Mesh and BLE development.

Specializing as a wireless engineer, you will work at a variety of levels: All the way from configuring RF to building Zephyr OS applications. The role centers on integrating and maintaining the ROM code split between 2 cores separating controller and host stack for BLE, and 802.15.4 controller and application. You will optimize the low-power scenarios to ensure very long lifetime of embedded devices by reducing battery consumption.

If you are an embedded developer at heart - comfortable with communication protocols and at home where hardware and software meet - this is the role for you to grow into

This is a permanent, full-time position for an engineer capable of independent planning, organizing, and executing their own work. The role does not require prior experience in a lead or managerial position but does require a strong sense of ownership and accountability.

The role will be built around the experience you have, but here’s some requirements that we feel may be beneficial for you to have:

* Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field

* Skilled in Embedded Software

* Experience in Low-level Embedded Software

* Proficiency in C

* Proficiency in Arm/Risc-V; familiarity with Verilog/SystemVerilog is a strong plus

* Experience with low-power design techniques

* Experience with wireless protocols and techniques

It would be great to have a teammate with good communication and problem-solving skills and the desire to seek diverse challenges to help you grow

We can promise you awesome challenges and great opportunities to grow, but we will also make sure you are compensated fairly and according to your seniority and our role expectations

The position is located in Oulu, Finland.

title: Control Panel Production Fabricator
description:

This is an hourly, full-time position requiring the ability to fabricate routine to complex panel assemblies from drawings and wiring schematics. Panels are used in the water treatment industry, helping our customers sustain an environmentally clean and stable global water supply.

Control Panel Production Fabricator must be able to interpret blueprints and follow work order instructions resulting in accurate assembly of components such as PLC’s, HMI’s, controllers, sensors, pumps, PVC pipe assemblies, etc. PLC assembly and/or wiring experience desired with UL508 Industrial Control Equipment knowledge (24VDC, 120VAC, 240VAC, motor controls). AquaPhoenix Scientific considers applicants with diverse backgrounds, education, and work experience; however, applicants for the Control Panel Production Fabricator will frequently have a combined education and/or work experience that is a minimum of a high school diploma or equivalent and at least three- five years’ work experience in a related industry that includes electrical, mechanical fabrication, plumping, water treatment, and similar manufacturing, and/or mechanical position.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
THIS ROLE MUST BE BASED IN THE SAN FRANCISCO BAY AREA (CALIFORNIA)

About OpenRouter

OpenRouter is the unified interface for AI inference, giving developers and organizations access to hundreds of models through a single API. Our platform helps teams choose, route, evaluate, and scale model usage across providers, making it easier to build production AI applications with the right model for every use case.

As inference becomes a core operating layer for modern software companies, OpenRouter helps customers move faster, reduce complexity, and get more value from the rapidly evolving model ecosystem.

About the Role

We are looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to join our post-sales team and help customers successfully implement, adopt, and scale OpenRouter.

This role sits at the intersection of customer success, support, customer engineering, product, and developer relations. You will work directly with our customers after the sale to help them get live quickly, integrate OpenRouter into production systems, improve their inference architecture, and expand usage across teams and applications.

You will be deeply hands-on with developers. You will debug integrations, design implementation paths, advise on model and routing strategy, identify opportunities to increase adoption, and turn customer learnings into product feedback. The ideal candidate is technical enough to earn the trust of engineering teams, commercial enough to understand customer outcomes, and proactive enough to drive customers from initial implementation to scaled production usage.

This role will require the ability to work regularly from our customers' offices across the San Francisco Bay Area and potentially travel to other locations as needed.

What You’ll Do

Customer Implementation

  • Lead technical onboarding for new customers after contract close, helping them move from kickoff to production usage.

  • Partner with Customer Success Managers and Account Executives to define success plans, implementation milestones, and technical adoption goals.

  • Help customers integrate OpenRouter into their applications, workflows, infrastructure, and developer environments.

  • Troubleshoot API, SDK, model selection, routing, latency, reliability, and deployment issues.

  • Create implementation guides, reference architectures, code examples, and reusable playbooks for common customer patterns.

Inference Adoption and Optimization

  • Work with customers to understand their AI use cases, application architecture, traffic patterns, and inference goals.

  • Recommend model, provider, routing, fallback, caching, and cost-optimization strategies based on customer needs.

  • Analyze usage patterns to identify opportunities to increase adoption, improve reliability, reduce cost, or expand into new workloads.

  • Help customers evaluate models and providers across quality, latency, cost, reliability, privacy, and scale requirements.

  • Drive customers from initial API usage to broader production deployment across teams and applications.

Technical and Developer Engagement

  • Build strong technical relationships with customer developers, engineering leaders, AI teams, and platform teams.

  • Run technical working sessions, integration reviews, architecture discussions, and developer enablement sessions.

  • Act as a trusted technical advisor for customers building AI-native products, agents, internal tools, and production LLM workflows.

  • Translate complex technical concepts into practical guidance for developers and business stakeholders.

  • Advocate for developer needs internally and help improve the customer implementation experience.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner closely with Customer Success to improve retention, adoption, customer health, and expansion.

  • Collaborate with Sales on technical expansion opportunities and strategic account growth.

  • Work with Product and Engineering to surface customer feedback, feature requests, integration blockers, and product gaps.

  • Contribute to internal knowledge bases, customer playbooks, onboarding materials, and best practices.

  • Help define what excellent post-sales technical engagement looks like at OpenRouter.

What We’re Looking For

  • 4+ years of experience in a technical customer-facing role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Solutions Architect, Technical Account Manager, Developer Advocate, or Customer Engineer.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and ability to read, write, and debug production-quality code.

  • Experience working with APIs, SDKs, cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, or AI/ML infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with LLMs, inference, model evaluation, prompt engineering, agents, latency/cost tradeoffs, and production AI application patterns.

  • Ability to work directly with developers and engineering leaders to diagnose problems and design practical solutions.

  • Strong customer instincts: you understand how to drive outcomes, manage ambiguity, and build trust.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially when explaining technical topics to mixed audiences.

  • High ownership, bias for action, and comfort operating in a fast-moving startup environment.

  • Ability to be on-site with customers regularly and travel to customer sites as needed.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with OpenAI-compatible APIs, model routing, evals, observability, or LLM application frameworks.

  • Prior experience in customer success, post-sales engineering, or implementation roles at an API, infrastructure, developer tools, or AI company.

  • Experience building AI agents, chat products, copilots, automation workflows, or production LLM applications.

  • Familiarity with Python, TypeScript, REST APIs, streaming APIs, and common backend application architectures.

  • Experience working with enterprise customers, startups, or technical founders.

  • Ability to create technical content such as guides, demos, example repos, migration docs, or architecture diagrams.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 30 days, you will learn OpenRouter’s product, customer base, implementation patterns, and post-sales motion. You will shadow customer calls, understand common integration paths, and begin supporting customer onboarding.

In your first 60 days, you will independently lead technical implementation workstreams, help customers resolve integration blockers, and contribute reusable technical assets for onboarding and adoption.

In your first 90 days, you will own technical success for a set of post-sales customers, drive measurable increases in production usage, identify expansion opportunities, and create a feedback loop between customers, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering.

You’ll Be a Great Fit If

  • You enjoy being close to customers and solving real-world implementation problems.

  • You are energized by helping developers ship faster and build better AI products.

  • You can go deep technically while staying focused on business outcomes.

  • You like operating across code, customer conversations, product feedback, and adoption strategy.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and can turn repeated customer problems into scalable systems, playbooks, and product insights.

  • You believe inference is becoming a foundational layer of software and want to help customers adopt it successfully.

If you don't think you meet all of the criteria below but still are interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we're looking for someone who is excited to join the team.

title: Sr. Specialist – Secondary ECU CICD Releases & Builds
description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

At Scout Motors, you don't just design vehicles- you shape the future of the road. Our Engineering team is where bold ideas meet rigorous execution, building machines that are as durable and capable as the people who drive them. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with brilliant minds across disciplines, turning complex challenges into elegant, scalable solutions that meet the highest standards of safety, performance, and user experience. This is a place where your fingerprints are found on metal – where what you design gets built, driven, and remembered. If you're hungry to engineer something that matters, Scout Motors is where that ambition finds its highest gear.

We are seeking a Senior Engineer to own CI/CD, Build Artifacts & Binary Release Engineering for Secondary ECUs to design, implement, and operate end-to-end software build and release systems for next-generation Software Defined Vehicle (SDV) architectures. This role focuses on binary generation, artifact management, build reproducibility, and CI/CD validation pipelines for distributed secondary ECUs across automotive domains such as body, energy, drive support systems, infotainment, connectivity, and gateways. You will own the integrity, traceability, and automation of ECU software delivery—from source code to signed production-ready binaries—across lab-car, HIL/SIL, integration vehicles, and production environments. This role will Q-gate, release secondary ECU artefacts per HPC compute and platform requirements directly shaping the reliability, scalability, and performance of the entire vehicle platform. Role is the backbone of software delivery for vehicle platforms ensuring ECU SW packages are reliably built, traceable, configurable, and deployable at scale enabling faster iteration, safer releases, and seamless integration across complex EV systems.

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

  • Design and maintain scalable build systems for secondary ECU software, ensuring deterministic and reproducible binary outputs.
  • Own end-to-end binary generation pipelines, including compilation, linking, packaging, and versioning for embedded ECUs.
  • Manage build configurations across multiple ECU variants, hardware revisions, and vehicle programs.
  • Ensure correct generation of firmware images, bootloaders, application binaries, calibration files, and configuration artifacts.
  • Optimize build performance, parallelization, caching strategies, and distributed build execution.
  • Own artifact lifecycle management including storage, versioning, traceability, and retention policies.
  • Manage software artifacts such as ECU firmware binaries, signed release packages, calibration datasets, configuration manifests, dependency graphs etc.
  • Implement strict traceability between source code → build → artifact → vehicle release.
  • Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines using tools like Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions
  • Implement pipelines for cross-compilation of embedded software, static analysis and validation checks with automated test execution (unit, integration, HIL where applicable)
  • Enable reproducible builds with traceability from commit → artifact → vehicle
  • Ensure secure and reliable delivery of artifacts to integration, vehicle builds, OTA systems and manufacturing pipelines
  • Develop tooling to generate custom ECU builds (feature flags, configuration variants, debug/release modes) and vehicle-level software packages (multi-ECU bundles) for on-demand builds for specific test or vehicle configurations
  • Coordinate release schedules and resolve integration issues

Location & Travel Expectations:

  • This role may be based out of the Scout Motors corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC.
  • This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.
  • Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

  • Master’s degree in electrical engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with 10+ yrs. of experience
  • Strong understanding of vehicle E/E architecture and ECU-level software stacks, automotive communication protocols (CAN, LIN, FlexRay, Ethernet), UDS diagnostics (ISO 14229) and diagnostic communication tools
  • Expert knowledge of Jira, GitHub/GitLab, Jenkins, and Artifactory. ALM/PLM proficiency in Siemens Polarion, IBM DOORS Next Gen, or PTC Windchill.
  • Strong understanding, development and verification of plant and control models in MATLAB/Simulink for execution in hardware in the loop test environment, dSpace control desk and automation desk
  • Strong understanding of 1st principles in Engineering, result/solution oriented.
  • Familiarity with SW for embedded systems, EE systems and architecture
  • Familiarity with A2B, CAN, Automotive Ethernet, LIN, LVDS communication protocols and Vehicle Network tools, such as CANalyzer, CANoe, etc.‚
  • Expertise with complex problem solving, data analysis, access/interpret/drive results with extended teams.
  • Knowledge of Automotive design and development process, system requirements, and general engineering best practices

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up. This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation. In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

  • Competitive insurance including:
    • Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans
  • 401(k) program with:
    • An employer match and immediate vesting
  • Generous Paid Time Off including:
    • 20 days planned PTO, as accrued
    • 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually
    • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders
    • Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $140,000.00 - $170,000.00

  • Residing in Los Angeles: Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.
  • Residing in New York City: This role is not eligible for remote work in New York City.

Job Title: Inventory Allocation & Batching Associate, Fulfillment

Department: GC Packaging Operations / Finished Goods Warehouse
Schedule: Hourly | Warehouse Operations| Second shift

Position Summary

The Inventory Allocation & Batching Associate, Fulfillment is an hourly warehouse Role, responsible for allocating inventory and creating pick jobs to support daily order fulfillment. This position works within Extensiv to organize orders by workstream, carrier ship method, and customer requirements, ensuring efficient picking, on-time shipment, and accurate inventory flow. The role partners closely with warehouse leadership, floor teams, and shipping to balance workload, meet carrier cutoffs, and support key operational performance metrics.

Key Responsibilities

  • Create and release pick batches in Extensiv by workstream, carrier ship method (Ground, Express, International, LTL, FTL), and customer, aligned to daily shipping cutoffs and labor capacity.
  • Prioritize batches to support ship-on-time performance, with emphasis on Express, International, and cutoff-driven orders.
  • Allocate inventory using established FIFO and location-based rules to reduce rework, shortages, and inventory discrepancies.
  • Post accurate and timely batch details to the Order Share list, ensuring real-time visibility across all active workstreams.
  • Communicate clearly with each workstream by providing a summarized pull list that includes order count, unit volume, priority level, and special handling requirements.
  • Monitor batch progress throughout the shift and proactively rebalance workload to prevent bottlenecks or missed SLAs.
  • Track and escalate unallocated, unreleased, or overdue orders within Order Management team to minimize fulfillment delays.
  • Identify and report inventory shortages, location errors, or system issues that impact picking efficiency or shipment timelines.

Support the Shipping Department as needed by:

  • Assisting with creation of Bills of Lading (BOLs) for LTL and FTL shipments.
  • Performing quality checks (QC) on LTL shipments to confirm pallet count, labels, documentation, and shipment accuracy prior to pickup.
  • Coordinating with shipping leads on carrier and driver scheduling when required to meet pickup windows and delivery commitments.
  • Maintain accurate batch and shipment status updates in Extensiv to support end-of-day closeout and reporting.
  • Support daily and weekly operational goals related to throughput, batch accuracy, ship-complete performance, and on-time pickup.
  • Follow all warehouse safety, quality, and standard operating procedures.

Qualifications

  • 1+ year of experience in warehouse operations, inventory management, order fulfillment, or shipping support.
  • Experience with a Warehouse Management System (Extensiv / 3PL Central strongly preferred).
  • Understanding of warehouse workflows including picking, staging, shipping, and carrier handoff.
  • Basic to intermediate proficiency in Excel and comfort working in computer-based systems.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and ability to follow standard operating procedures.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and work effectively in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
  • Reliable attendance and ability to work assigned schedule.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Working knowledge of FIFO and location-based inventory allocation strategies.
  • Experience supporting LTL/FTL shipping processes, BOL creation, or carrier coordination.
  • Experience in wholesale or finished goods warehouse operations.

title: Head of Commercial Finance
description:
🌍 London (Old Street, 3 days/week)

🤝 Reports to: FD

🔎 Level: Senior

We're not just closing the digital divide; we're reconnecting distributed organisations, enabling seamless communication, and re-engaging employees like never before. Blink, a mobile-first employee experience platform, puts everything employees need right in their hands. With teams in Boston, London, and Sydney, we're making waves worldwide, partnering with industry leaders like Domino's, JD Sports and McDonald's.

The Role

You'll be the FD's right hand. Not a narrow commercial or FP&A seat, but the person who picks up whatever moves the function forward, from the strategic and forward-looking work through to the operational plumbing that keeps the close clean.

On any given week that might mean owning a pricing decision, framing a capital allocation trade-off, sharpening a process the close team relies on, or building an agent that takes work off everyone's plate. You'll partner with the exec team on the decisions that shape Blink's next stage of growth, and you'll work shoulder to shoulder with the existing finance team on the day-to-day. The remit flexes to what the business needs, and you're someone who's energized by that rather than thrown by it.

What you'll own

Forecasting and FP&A

  • Forecasting infrastructure owned by finance end to end.
  • Reporting rhythms the business actually uses.
  • Ownership of finance and commercial analytics, the FinOps stack, and data quality.

Finance operations and process

  • Being a strong and innovative partner with the rest of the finance team, assisting them to design and tighten processes across the function that help to scale systems and operations.
  • A genuine willingness to pick up what's needed, with no task seen as beneath the role.
  • Improving the speed and accuracy of close and multi-entity reporting frameworks .

AI and finance operations

  • The agentic finance stack from FP&A augmentation through close acceleration, variance commentary, and scenario modelling.
  • Project management of digital transformation: partnering with the team to implement systems.
  • Billing agents that cut cycle time and tighten cash conversion.
  • Tooling selection across subscriptions, ERP, expense, AP, consolidation.
  • Mentoring the wider finance team on agent design so the capability scales.
  • SaaS metrics (NRR, GRR, CAC, payback, magic number, unit economics by segment and product) used to shape forecasts and investments.

Projects you’ll work on

Commercial

  • Pricing and packaging end to end, from new-product pricing and bundle design to renewal pricing and discount discipline.
  • Value realisation frameworks across the sales and CS lifecycle.
  • Direct support on strategic deals, renewals, and contract restructures.

Strategic

  • Capital allocation: framing trade-offs, owning the numbers, presenting options.
  • The annual operating plan and budget, end to end.
  • Headcount and capacity modeling with leadership and People Ops.
  • Investment cases for major bets, each with a clear recommendation.
  • Strategic and commercial sections of the board pack.
  • Fundraising and debt financing alongside the FD: model, materials, diligence, banker engagement, term negotiation.

Requirements

Who you are

Background

  • 6 to 8 years in consulting, investment, banking, strategic FP&A, or BizOps, with high-growth SaaS or PLG exposure.
  • You've owned pricing, unit economics, and the commercial finance conversation end to end.
  • You’re comfortable in the room with the C-suite, and equally happy in the detail of a close.
  • You've been part of a fundraise or material debt financing.
  • You've built or scaled an FP&A function in a high-growth environment — you know what good infrastructure looks like and you've done the work to get it there, not just inherited it.

Technical depth

  • Investor-grade financial modelling: three-statement, scenario, cohort, unit economics.
  • SQL fluency.
  • Working knowledge of the modern SaaS finance stack (Chargebee, Xero, HubSpot, Snowflake, ThoughtSpot or equivalent).
  • ACA, ACCA, CIMA OR CFA qualified.

AI build

  • You've shipped at least one end-to-end agentic workflow in a finance context and can walk us through the design, control surface, evidence trail, and measurable outcome.
  • You've used Claude, OpenAI, or similar APIs in production, not just chat.

Working style

  • Commercial reasoning and influence, not just analysis.
  • Genuine ownership: you take a remit and run it, you don't draw hard lines around what's "your job".
  • Comfortable spanning the strategic and the operational, and switching between them in a day
  • A builder of processes and a team player who makes the people around them better
  • Cross-functional credibility
  • Comfort with ambiguity, because you'll define some of this as you go

Year-one success

  • Pricing and packaging owned end to end, with at least one material change that moves revenue or NRR.
  • Forecasting infrastructure live, trusted, and improving quarter over quarter.
  • At least two agentic workflows live in production with documented cycle-time or accuracy gains.
  • The annual operating plan and budget owned end to end with cross-functional sign-off.
  • Board pack strategic and commercial sections drafted by you.
  • Tangible improvements to the close and core finance processes, made hand in hand with the existing team.

Benefits

You will have the opportunity to be part of something impactful, large-scale, and meaningful. Most importantly, you’ll work for a company with a strong purpose, with an ambitious team embarking on a journey most start-ups can only dream of!

Benefits include 💚

    • A small, senior, ambitious finance team, with exec visibility from week one
    • The ability to design the agentic finance stack from scratch in collaboration with the team.
    • Competitive salary.
    • Stock options on starting and additional high performer grants annually!
    • 25 days’ leave + public holidays.
    • Additional time off between Christmas and New Year.
    • Private healthcare with AXA.
    • 3% employer pension contribution when you contribute 5%.
    • Cycle to Work scheme.
    • Social events ( lunches, breakfasts, nights out).
    • Enhanced parental leave.

At Blink, we're committed to creating an inclusive and diverse culture where our people feel they truly belong. We value and respect individual differences, so all applications will receive fair and equal consideration without regard to ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, nationality, disability or age

title: Senior Security Engineer
description:
About the Role

  • The Senior Security Engineer is the enterprise security Subject Matter Expert (SME) for identity, messaging, authentication, monitoring and security integrations. The role provides strategic security input, develops technical designs, secure integration, documentation and operational governance of Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, Exchange, Microsoft Sentinel, Silverfort, PKI, DNS and related enterprise services.
  • The role provides security expertise for business-critical application integrations, including Microsoft 365, Azure, HR, ERP and third-party platforms, ensuring secure access, provisioning, logging, monitoring, resilience and compliance closely working with security partners and internal IT teams.
  • Key Responsibilities
  • Security Partnerships
  • Partner with internal cybersecurity teams, external security vendors, technology partners, and business stakeholders to design, implement, and continuously improve enterprise security controls and capabilities.
  • Implementation of NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) and industry security best practices across identity, cloud, infrastructure, messaging, monitoring, and business application platforms.
  • Assess security risks, recommend remediation strategies, and lead the implementation of security improvements, ensuring alignment with enterprise security standards, compliance requirements, and Zero Trust principles.
  • Identity & Access Security
  • Own Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure AD Connect and cloud synchronization architecture, health and security.
  • Manage identity automation scripts, Administrative Units, RBAC, Conditional Access, MFA, domains, trusts and privileged access controls.
  • Design secure SSO, authentication, user lifecycle and provisioning integrations for Microsoft 365 and other enterprise applications.
  • Validate service accounts, API permissions, role mappings, access reviews and joiner-mover-leaver controls for integrated platforms.
  • Security Platforms
  • Lead Microsoft Sentinel management, documentation, data onboarding, detection use cases, workbooks and operational support.
  • Integrate and monitor logs from Domain Controllers, Azure, Exchange, servers, applications and security platforms.
  • Define logging, retention, alerting, incident workflow and operational runbook standards.
  • Tune analytics rules and dashboards to improve detection quality, investigation and response.
  • Effective use of Microsoft Security Copilot and AI-powered security capabilities to improve threat detection, investigation, and incident response.
  • Evaluate, secure, and govern AI integrations and enterprise AI solutions, ensuring compliance with security, privacy, identity, and NIST best practices.
  • Silverfort & Authentication Security
  • Serve as the Silverfort SME, platform owner and primary technical point of contact.
  • Design, build, configure and operate Silverfort nodes in Azure and hybrid environments.
  • Manage integrations, authentication policies, licensing, vendor engagement, upgrades, health monitoring, high availability and recovery testing.
  • Messaging, PKI & Enterprise Services
  • Provide security oversight for Exchange Online, Hybrid Exchange, load balancers, mail flow, Exchange rules and Teams integrations.
  • Manage Enterprise Certificate Authority, public certificates, PKI, KMS and certificate lifecycle controls.
  • Oversee public DNS, domain registration and deregistration, billing, DMARC, SPF and DKIM.
  • Architecture, Integration & Governance
  • Act as the security design authority and SME for cloud, identity, HR, ERP, business application and third-party integrations.
  • Review authentication, authorization, data flows, APIs, service principals, service accounts, certificates, and SIEM logging.
  • Maintain reference architectures, diagrams, standards, runbooks, dependency maps and recovery procedures.
  • Support audits, compliance reviews, security incidents, platform upgrades and Domain Controller post-upgrade testing.

Experience:

  • 6 - 8years of experience in security engineering, identity, infrastructure security or security architecture.
  • Strong expertise in Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure AD Connect, Exchange, Microsoft Sentinel, Silverfort, PKI and Azure security.
  • Experience securing SaaS and enterprise integrations, Microsoft 365, HR and ERP platforms.
  • Working knowledge of SAML, OAuth/OIDC, APIs, Microsoft Graph, service principles, certificates and privileged access controls.
  • Proficiency in PowerShell automation, SIEM integration, troubleshooting, and security documentation.
  • Desirable certifications: CISSP, CISM, SC-100, SC-300, SC-200 or AZ-500.
  • Success Measures
  • Secure and reliable operation of identity, messaging, Sentinel and Silverfort platforms.
  • Secure, documented and supportable integrations
  • Complete SIEM visibility across identity, cloud, messaging, Domain Controllers and priority infrastructure.
  • Current architecture diagrams, runbooks, ownership records and knowledge-transfer documentation.
  • Improved security posture, authentication resilience, audit readiness and operational recovery.

Key Technologies

Entra ID | Active Directory | Azure AD Connect | Microsoft Sentinel | Silverfort | Exchange Online | Teams | NetSuite | SuitePeople | PKI | DNS | DMARC | Azure | PowerShell | Microsoft Graph | SAML | OAuth/OIDC | SCIM | SSO | MFA | Conditional Access | KMS

Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

At Scout Motors, you don't just design vehicles- you shape the future of the road. Our Engineering team is where bold ideas meet rigorous execution, building machines that are as durable and capable as the people who drive them. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with brilliant minds across disciplines, turning complex challenges into elegant, scalable solutions that meet the highest standards of safety, performance, and user experience. This is a place where your fingerprints are found on metal – where what you design gets built, driven, and remembered. If you're hungry to engineer something that matters, Scout Motors is where that ambition finds its highest gear.

As HiL and Requirements Coordinator – Drive Systems, you will combine two critical responsibilities in one role:

  1. Coordinating all Hardware‑in‑the‑Loop (HiL) activities for BEV and REEV drive‑system components
  1. Owning the requirements and test‑case management processes for the drive system, ensuring quality, maturity, and transparency across development phases

This role is central to ensuring functional correctness, software quality, and release readiness for the Scout drive system. Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

HiL Coordination Responsibilities

  • Coordinate all HiL activities within the drive system for BEV and REEV components, acting as the central interface between software development, function owners, calibration, testing, and systems engineering teams
  • Plan, steer, and supervise HiL test execution, ensuring test environments, configurations, software builds, and test content are available and aligned with program priorities
  • Coordinate the HiL execution team responsible for test implementation and execution, providing clear scope, priorities, test objectives, and acceptance criteria
    This role focuses on coordination and governance rather than hands‑on test development or scripting.
  • Define and align HiL test strategies for drive‑system functions, covering operating strategies, diagnostics, fault reactions, degraded modes, and system‑level integration behavior
  • Track HiL execution progress, manage dependencies, identify risks or bottlenecks, and drive timely resolution in collaboration with function and validation stakeholders
  • Ensure HiL activities are aligned across prototype and serial development phases, supporting integration milestones, validation reviews, and software release readiness

Requirements & Test‑Case Coordination Responsibilities

  • Own and oversee drive‑system requirements management, including:
  • Reviewing completeness, clarity, and consistency of functional and system requirements
  • Ensuring requirements follow defined development processes and quality standards
  • Tracking requirement maturity, changes, and status throughout development
  • Coordinate and control drive‑system test‑case management, ensuring:
  • Test cases are correctly derived from requirements and acceptance criteria
  • Coverage, execution status, and results are monitored across HiL activities
  • Traceability is maintained between requirements, test cases, and validation outcomes
  • Assess and monitor the quality of the underlying processes for requirements and test‑case management, identifying gaps, risks, or inconsistencies and driving corrective actions
  • Provide structured and transparent status reporting on HiL progress, requirements maturity, and test‑case coverage to support technical and program decision making

Cross‑Functional Collaboration & Support

  • Liaise closely with function development, calibration, systems architecture, and validation teams to align priorities, resolve issues, and support integration decisions
  • Support technical discussions by reviewing test results, contributing to root‑cause analysis, and coordinating follow‑up testing or fixes
  • Coordinate software and function readiness in support of prototype builds, validation phases, and release milestones
  • Support additional related tasks and activities required to ensure robust drive‑system validation and timely delivery

Location & Travel Expectations:

  • This role will be based out of the Scout Motors location in Novi, Michigan.
  • This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.
  • Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Technology, IT Systems, or Engineering Technology from an accredited college or university; preferably Electrical, Controls, or Automotive Engineering
  • 8+ years of experience in automotive concept or serial development, with prior hands‑on experience in HiL test development, scripting, or execution earlier in the career
  • Strong practical understanding of HiL architectures, test implementation, automation concepts, and execution workflows, enabling effective coordination and technical judgment
    (Current role focus is on coordination, oversight, and process governance rather than hands‑on development.)
  • Solid understanding of requirements engineering and test‑case management, including traceability, maturity tracking, and process quality
  • Experience working within system engineering, integration, validation, and software release processes
  • Proven coordination and project‑steering skills, with the ability to manage execution performed by other teams
  • Structured, quality‑focused mindset with strong analytical and problem‑solving skills
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across cross‑functional and global teams

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up. This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation. In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

  • Competitive insurance including:
    • Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans
  • 401(k) program with:
    • An employer match and immediate vesting
  • Generous Paid Time Off including:
    • 20 days planned PTO, as accrued
    • 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually
    • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders
    • Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $120,000.00 - $145,000.00

  • Residing in Los Angeles: Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.
  • Residing in New York City: This role is not eligible for remote work in New York City.

title: SAP Finance Functional Analyst

  • Lead the migration and configuration of SAP Central Finance (CFIN) to enable real-time data consolidation and harmonized reporting across the enterprise.
  • Establish and maintain Payment Factory workflows to automate high-volume transaction processing and reduce manual intervention.
  • Develop and troubleshoot Banking Integrations and Electronic Bank Statement (EBS) feeds to ensure seamless data exchange with external financial institutions.

Requirements

Requirements:
  • Minimum of 5 years of hands-on experience within the IT Services sector, specifically focusing on SAP Finance solutions.
  • Proven expertise in SAP FSCM, including BCM and BAM configurations.
  • Deep functional knowledge of In-House Cash, In-House Banking, and Payment Factory architectures.
  • Strong proficiency in managing FX Rate Integrations and SAP Treasury and Risk Management (TRM) modules.
  • Demonstrated experience with SAP Central Finance (CFIN) implementation and support.
  • Solid background in configuring Banking Integrations and processing Electronic Bank Statements.
  • Ability to translate complex business requirements into precise technical specifications and solutions.
