title: Quality Assurance Specialist (Non-Profit) - New York City
description:
AHRC NYC is seeking a Quality Assurance Specialist for their Hudson River division. The Quality Assurance Manager conducts field inspections and process compliance reviews to verify that HRS services meet contract specifications and that managers and supervisors follow established procedures. The position completes and documents inspections, reports deficiencies, tracks required actions and manager progress, and verifies that corrections are completed and sustained. This work supports HRS’s Quality Assurance Plan and Cleaning Industry Management Standard (CIMS) processes.

Compensation Package: $66,300 per year plus a very generous and comprehensive Benefit package. See Benefit information below.

Schedule: Monday through Friday 9am-5pm....35 hours per week.

Summary of Position

Quality Assurance Manager works under the direction of the Regional Manager QA and coordinates with Regional Managers, Assistant Regional Managers, site managers, forepersons, and other designated staff. The position monitors and verifies service quality and procedural compliance. Managers and supervisors remain responsible for daily operations, employee supervision, and implementation of corrective actions.

A minimum of 80% of work time is expected in the field at HRS service locations. Field work includes scheduled and unannounced visits, quality inspections, review of site records, observation of employee work, and verification of Regional Manager follow-through. The remaining time supports reporting, inspection planning, and tracking outstanding actions. Work schedules must be flexible to observe services during early morning, evening, overnight, and weekend hours as assigned. May be necessary to back up operations when directed.

HRS craftsmanship means understanding the work, taking pride in how it is performed, and accepting quality as the finished product. This position reinforces that standard through objective observation, clear reporting, consistent follow-up, and respectful interactions with employees, including employees with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Quality inspections and service verification

  • Conduct scheduled and unannounced inspections at assigned accounts using the approved HRS Quality Assurance Plan, contract scope of work, service frequencies, and inspection criteria.
  • Complete accurate inspections in Janitorial Manager using approved templates and scoring standards. Record specific observations, locations, and supporting photographs when appropriate and permitted.
  • Inspect routine cleaning, periodic services, floor care, and other assigned work for completeness and quality. Compare observed conditions with contract requirements and approved work schedules.
  • Observe employee work practices and verify adherence to assigned tasks, work instructions, customer service expectations, and applicable uniform requirements. Report discrepancies to the responsible manager.
  • Monitor whether responsible managers complete required weekly inspections and other assigned QA activities. Identify missed or incomplete inspections and report them to the Regional Manager QA.

Process and procedure compliance

  • Review worker schedules for accuracy, completeness, availability at the site, and alignment with approved service requirements. Compare scheduled coverage with observed staffing and report unaddressed gaps or discrepancies.
  • Review sign-in sheets for required entries, completeness, legibility, and consistency with schedules and observed attendance. Identify missing entries, unexplained changes, and other discrepancies; refer issues for management review and resolution.
  • Verify that employees follow approved attendance, clock-in and clock-out, and call-out procedures through observation and authorized review of records. Report discrepancies through established channels; payroll corrections and formal personnel actions remain with authorized staff.
  • Check periodic service schedules and completion records. Verify that required work is performed, documented, and followed up when delayed or missed.
  • Review site operations and Communication Log Books for current scopes of work, worker schedules, periodic schedules, site maps, contact and escalation information, sign-in materials, applicable instructions, and QA records.
  • Check assigned procedural records, including inventory logs, equipment inventories, order documentation, and training completion records, against approved HRS requirements. Report missing, outdated, or inconsistent information.
  • Use approved checklists to verify implementation of assigned CIMS-related procedures. Compare documented requirements with actual site practice and maintain factual evidence of compliance or deficiencies.

Deficiency reporting and management follow through

  • Report deficiencies promptly to the responsible Regional Manager and Regional Manager QA. Describe the requirement, observed condition, location, and evidence clearly so the manager can determine and implement the correction.
  • Maintain a tracking record of findings, responsible managers, agreed actions, due dates, status, and follow-up results. Track regional manager progress on corrective actions and assigned process requirements.
  • Conduct follow-up visits or review appropriate supporting records to verify completion. Close findings only when the correction has been verified; document recurring issues and ineffective corrections.
  • Escalate overdue actions, repeated deficiencies, missed inspections, and unresolved procedural gaps to the Regional Manager QA and Director of Operations.
  • Identify patterns across accounts, including recurring service deficiencies, schedule discrepancies, incomplete records, and missed periodic work. Provide evidence-based observations to support management decisions.
  • Communicate professionally with employees and managers. Seek clarification of observed discrepancies, respect employee dignity, and maintain confidentiality of personnel and customer information.

Reporting and QA coordination

  • Plan field visits with the Regional Manager QA based on assigned accounts, inspection requirements, outstanding findings, customer concerns, and identified performance gaps.
  • Keep inspection records and action trackers current in Janitorial Manager and other approved HRS systems. Maintain organized, traceable records that support internal reviews and CIMS assessments.
  • Provide regular summaries to the Regional Manager QA covering inspection completion, quality results, procedural compliance, regional manager progress, overdue actions, and recurring findings.
  • Support QA team reviews and CIMS evidence collection within assigned responsibilities. Recommend improvements to inspection checklists or reporting methods when requirements or service conditions change.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned within the position’s quality inspection, procedural compliance, reporting, and follow-up responsibilities.

Performance Expectations

  • Maintain the minimum 80% field presence and complete assigned inspections and compliance reviews on schedule.
  • Produce accurate, objective, complete inspection records and timely deficiency reports.
  • Keep Regional Manager action status current, verify completion by agreed due dates, and escalate unresolved issues.
  • Identify repeat deficiencies and procedural gaps using consistent criteria and reliable evidence.
  • Maintain organized QA documentation and provide timely progress summaries to the Regional Manager QA.

Specific inspection coverage, reporting frequency, and follow-up targets are established by the Regional Manager QA.

  • Experience in commercial cleaning or facility services, including inspection, site supervision, quality assurance, or comparable field responsibilities. Experience working across multiple accounts is preferred.
  • Knowledge of cleaning methods, floor care, service frequencies, contract scopes of work, worker schedules, and site documentation. Familiarity with CIMS processes is preferred.
  • Ability to observe work objectively, apply inspection criteria consistently, identify discrepancies, maintain accurate records, and follow assignments through completion.
  • Ability to use Janitorial Manager or comparable inspection software, email, spreadsheets, and electronic action trackers; willingness and ability to learn HRS systems.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, effective organization, sound judgment, and the ability to work independently under the direction of the Regional Manager QA.
  • Ability to work respectfully with employees with intellectual and developmental disabilities, employment support staff, managers, and customers.
  • Must hold a valid New York State driver’s license and have held that license for at least one year. Must comply with AHRC NYC driving requirements.
  • Must have a personal vehicle available for business travel and maintain required vehicle registration and insurance consistent with agency policy. Authorized business use of the personal vehicle will be reimbursed in accordance with AHRC NYC reimbursement policy.
  • Ability to travel throughout the assigned HRS service area and work a flexible schedule to inspect services during the hours they are performed.
  • Low cost, high quality Medical Insurance (Single & Family Plans)
  • Paid time off (sick, personal & vacation)
  • Paid Training

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.

But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.

Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.

title: Dietary Assistant II
description:
Sisters of the Holy Cross is accepting applications for two part-time (24 hours a week) Dietary Assistant II position.


Main Function:

Participates with others in the preparation and serving of food and beverages, assists with stocking food items and supplies in work areas, and always follows sanitary guidelines.



ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS


  1. Completes the processing of produce, the preparation of salads, the assembly of meal trays, table service in the dining room, and the processing of menus.
  2. Under supervision, assures that all areas of dietary responsibilities are met in a timely and sanitary manner.
  3. Assures that all necessary dietary equipment, utensils and food contact surfaces are clean, sanitized, and ready for use.
  4. Prepare food and beverages according to menus/production sheets.
  5. Ensure that prepared, served items are attractive and correctly portioned.
  6. Keep work areas well stocked with food items and supplies as specified.
  7. Arranges and restocks serving areas (food, beverages, salads, clean dishes and utensils).
  8. Follows food safety and sanitation guidelines consistently.
  9. Sweep and maintain floors as assigned.
  10. Assembly and delivery of catering orders.
  11. Documents required temperatures (foods, equipment, etc.) and alerts manager to irregularities.
  12. Follows instructions and safety rules when working with cleaning products.
  13. Duties require lifting to 50 pounds. Always maintain safe techniques.
  14. Maintains attendance and observes working hours, starting time, lunch period, breaks, quitting time, etc.
  15. Complies with work rules, regulations, and instructions, follows established systems and procedures, completes assignments with minimal supervision.
  16. Serve hot food in the dining room and cold food on the salad bar.
  17. Help with serving drinks and ice cream in the dining room.
  18. Work any position on tray line as scheduled.
  19. Tally menus from the convent floors.
  20. Prep items to be served on the tray line.
  21. Being able to alternate items for allergies and intolerances.
  22. Puree items as needed.
  23. Work hand in hand with the cook and salad to discuss items on the menus.
  24. Help in the dish area as needed.
  25. Clear tables in the dining room.
  26. Clean, sanitize and reset tables.
  27. Check food on tray line to ensure the Sisters are receiving the correct diet and the items they requested .
  28. Any other duties as assigned by Nutrition Services management.



MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education

High school diploma preferred.


Experience

One (1) year of relevant experience in an institutional setting is preferred.


Responsibility

Must be able to follow policies and procedures relating to food service, especially in sanitation. Adverse decisions may impact the quality, timeliness of meals and services. Requires the ability to properly follow written instructions in all areas of responsibility.

Problem-Solving

Problems require solutions based on knowledge and good judgment.


Personal Interaction

Internal communications with Nutrition Services staff and residents. Additional interactions with guests of the sisters and volunteers.


Work Environment

Pleasant work environment.


Equipment Utilization

Requires operating knowledge of food service equipment such as oven, blender, food processor, toaster, coffee maker, etc.


Hazards or Fatigue

Ordinary care and caution must be exercised while performing work activities. Duties require lifting to 50 pounds.


Planning and Organizing

Works on a daily and weekly schedule under supervision.


Directing and Instructing

Not required.


Budgeting

Not required.


Scope of Supervision

Not required.

description:

title: Head, Collections, UK/Europe
description:
ABOUT TIDE

At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.

Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, India, Germany and France.

Using advanced technology, all solutions are designed with SMEs in mind. With quick onboarding, low fees and innovative features, we thrive on making data driven decisions to serve our mission: to help SMEs save time and money so they can get back to doing what they love.

Tide facts:

  • Tide is available for UK, Indian, German and French SMEs
  • Over 2 million members globally and rapidly growing
  • Over $300 million raised in funding
  • 3,000 Tideans globally
  • Recognised with Great Place to Work certification three years in a row, and among India’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance in 2026
  • We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Head of Member Collections (UK/Europe) reporting to the SVP, Member Operations (UK/Europe). Tide has a number of different lending portfolios that it offers to its small-business (SME) Members, including a BBLS book. Tide primarily intermediates credit through its wholly-owned Funding Options Business. Tide Capital, our proprietary credit business, focuses on transactional credit allowing Members to finance payment transactions. CreditFlex allows Members to finance payments in the payment flow. Tide is one of the larger issuers of commercial cards and, in due course, a credit card option will be offered to eligible Members using Tide Expense Cards. Collections also supports the management of negative balances that can arise from our regular Tide Expense Card transactions, e.g. via chargebacks. We are looking for an experienced operational leader to own and deliver Tide’s collections strategy to optimise the value of these portfolios.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Lead a small but growing team of collections manager & specialists spread between our Operations in the UK, Bulgaria and India.
  • Be willing and able to work iteratively between strategy and hands-on operational performance management required at a scale-up like Tide.
  • Be part of the leadership team of Member Operations and work closely with other Member-facing teams, including Member Support, KYX, Ongoing Monitoring and Complaints.
  • Shape the strategic direction for Collections at Tide, liaising closely with other relevant stakeholders in Risk & Compliance (2LOD), Tide Credit Services (Tide Capital), Finance and Legal.
  • Optimise recovery rates through process optimisation and forbearing solutions whilst also ensuring we treat Members fairly, recognise vulnerability and operate in accordance with Tide’s policies and industry best practice.
  • Own Tide’s relationship with debt collection agencies, overseeing their performance, assessing current contracts and reviewing future opportunities and alternatives.
  • Work closely with the product and data teams and third-party suppliers to improve our collections tools and processes, to optimise both Member experience and operational efficiency. Where possible, unnecessary manual processes should be automated.
  • Work closely with the data team to improve management reporting and ensure robust data is used to provide insight and support decisions.
  • Work closely with Talent and People partners and subject-matter trainers to ensure we continue to recruit, upskill and retain the very best employees at Tide.

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF:

  • You have hands-on experience working as a collections leader, particularly related to small business or consumer lending in the UK, and have extensive subject matter expertise. Ideally this includes government-backed and unsecured loan portfolios.
  • You are passionate about credit collections and can articulate your philosophy of how to optimise recovery rates, while also providing a great Member experience.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced and innovative environment and ideally have experience working in a Fintech. You are comfortable with a ‘test & learn’ approach to improving collection and recovery rates.
  • You have proven leadership and management experience and a track record of communicating clear strategic objectives and plans, and delivering on those plans. Ideally you will also have experience of working with outsourced collections teams.
  • You have experience of working with product and data teams, and are able to clearly articulate your requirements and vision.
  • You have an in-depth knowledge of all risk factors in collections and recovery processes and ways to mitigate them.
  • You are data driven and comfortable with OKRs, KPIs, KRIs, SLAs, forecasting, budgeting and planning.
  • You are a positive individual, with a flexible and creative mind and aim to bring out the best in people around you.
  • You naturally align with our values (#MemberFirst, #OneTeam, #DataDriven)


WHAT YOU’LL GET IN RETURN:

Make work, work for you! We are embracing new ways of working and support flexible working arrangements. With our Working Out of Office (WOO) policy our colleagues can work remotely from home or anywhere in their home country. Additionally, you can work from a different country for 90 days of the year. Plus, you’ll get:

  • Competitive salary
  • Self & Family Health Insurance
  • Term & Life Insurance
  • OPD Benefits
  • Mental wellbeing through Plumm
  • Learning & Development Budget
  • WFH Setup allowance
  • 15 days of Privilege leaves
  • 12 days of Casual leaves
  • 12 days of Sick leaves
  • 3 paid days off for volunteering or L&D activities
  • Stock Options

TIDEAN WAYS OF WORKING

At Tide, we champion a flexible workplace model that supports both in-person and remote work to cater to the specific needs of our different teams.

While remote work is supported, we believe in the power of face-to-face interactions to foster team spirit and collaboration. Our offices are designed as hubs for innovation and team-building, where we encourage regular in-person gatherings to foster a strong sense of community.

TIDE IS A PLACE FOR EVERYONE

At Tide, we believe that we can only succeed if we let our differences enrich our culture. Our Tideans come from a variety of backgrounds and experience levels. We consider everyone irrespective of their ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran, neurodiversity or differently-abled status. We celebrate diversity in our workforce as a cornerstone of our success. Our commitment to a broad spectrum of ideas and backgrounds is what enables us to build products that resonate with our members’ diverse needs and lives.

We are One Team and foster a transparent and inclusive environment, where everyone’s voice is heard.

At Tide, we thrive on diversity, embracing various backgrounds and experiences. We welcome all individuals regardless of ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability. Our inclusive culture is key to our success, helping us build products that meet our members' diverse needs. We are One Team, committed to transparency and ensuring everyone’s voice is heard.

Disclaimer
It has come to our attention that individuals or agencies are falsely claiming to represent Tide and are reaching out to candidates regarding job opportunities. Please be aware that:
  • Tide does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process.
  • All official Tide job opportunities are listed exclusively on our Careers Page and applications should be submitted through this channel.
  • Communication from Tide will only come from an official @tide.co email address.
  • Tide does not work with agencies or recruiters without prior formal engagement, and we do not authorize third parties to make job offers on our behalf.

If you are contacted by anyone misrepresenting Tide or requesting payment, please treat it as fraudulent and report it to us immediately at talent@tide.co
Your safety and trust are important to us, and we are committed to ensuring a fair and transparent recruitment process.

Tide leverages AI to enhance our hiring experience. You can read more about how we use AI in our recruitment process in our AI Policy.

Your personal data will be processed by Tide for recruitment purposes and in accordance with Tide's Recruitment Privacy Notice.

title: Director, Social Services (Lenox)
description:
PRIMARY FUNCTION/PURPOSE:

The Assistant Program Director is to assist the Program Director with the oversight and management of all shelter sites within assigned region. The Assistant Director will provide leadership in directing services and support to all clients and staff to ensure social services and operational procedures are being followed and seek improvement regarding those procedures throughout the entire shelter.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Oversee housing team while providing motivational, strength-based supervision to ensure quarterly placement targets are met.
  • Identify, collaborate, and foster long term relationships with realtors and property managers to locate and retain housing for families in temporary shelter. Monitor participants’ compliance with locating, obtaining, and retaining suitable housing.
  • Facilitate case conferences and ensure Social Service Supervisors and Case Managers develop individualized housing and service plans, including paths to housing stability.
  • Promote linkage with other service providers that will help participants secure the resources needed to obtain and maintain permanent housing.
  • Provide individual and group supervision to Social Service Supervisors, Case Managers and Housing Specialists.
  • Review housing packages for consistency and accuracy prior to submitting to DHS for review/approval.
  • Review and ensures proper documentation in CARES, including progress notes, Shelter Assessments, Service Plans and Case Conferences.
  • Monitor and document staff and client compliance with CRF, DHS and OTDA policies and procedures.
  • Conduct periodic internal file reviews and implement Quality Assurance measures to ensure compliance with CRF, DHS and OTDA standards.
  • Maintain case and agency paperwork according to CRF, DHS and OTDA standards.
  • Monitor client databases; ensure timely entry of data according to CRF, DHS and OTDA.
  • Evaluate staff work, complete performance evaluations to assess compliance with mandates. Initiate disciplinary/corrective action when needed.
  • Attend Family Team Conferences, Elevated Risk Conferences and Child Safety Conferences to maintain case focus and direction; facilitates conferences as needed.
  • Attend all required DHS meetings.
  • Report serious incidents to DHS Serious Incident Hotline in a timely manner and in accordance with DHS/OTDA mandates.
  • Ensure all incidents are documented in CARES and submitted to DHS for review/approval as prescribed by DHS.
  • Support the Program Director in overall management of the program.
  • Assist with compilation and/or distribution DHS Demographics, Exit, PA engagement and School Attendance reports.
  • Distribute relevant and pertinent data to all staff lines as needed.
  • Ensure reports are completed and submitted to DHS in a timely manner.
  • Represent region on DHS conference calls as needed.
  • In the absence of the Program Director, assumes roles and responsibilities of the Program Director.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Work or related field required.
  • At least three (3) years of organizational and supervisory experience working in the field of social service, housing or emergency shelter.
  • Experience with single and/or multi-problem families desirable.
  • Ability to think and act calmly in emergency situations.
  • Ability to work with a team.
  • Attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with ability to manage tasks efficiently.
  • Excellent time management skills with ability to prioritize assignments.
  • Excellent analytical, evaluative, and human service management skills.
  • Excellent written and oral communication, organizational, supervisory, and leadership skills.
  • Must have incredible initiative, the ability to work well under pressure, and the ability to be flexible and work both independently and as part of a team to complete complex projects in a fast-paced environment.
  • Must be adept and comfortable with crisis management.
  • Demonstrated experience working in shelter setting and/or with high-risk families, including families with documented histories mental health, substance abuse, Domestic Violence, child abuse/neglect.
  • Ability to work effectively with a wide range of community-based providers.
  • Working knowledge of Case Management theories and approaches.
  • Knowledge of community health services, social service support agencies and networks.
  • Familiarity with DHS and OTDA social service documentation policies and procedures. Critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills as well as resourcefulness.
  • High level of computer proficiency in Word, Excel, and the ability to learn new technologies and databases.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of and proficiency in CARES.
  • Bilingual in Spanish preferred.

Other Requirements (including Physical Demands)

  • Travel required.
  • May be required to work long hours and a varied schedule.
  • Lifting and moving objects weighing up to 30 pounds several times a week.
  • Climatic issues of temperature variance and ventilation association with resident facility impact delivery of services.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

EEO Statement – Children’s Rescue Fund is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation or protected veteran status.

title: Contracts Coordinator
description:
Life.Church wants to make a lasting difference in your life, in our community, and in the world. Our mission is to lead people to become fully devoted followers of Christ. That's how we’re able to make a difference, and it's the driving force behind everything we do.
The Contracts Coordinator is primarily responsible for reviewing, analyzing, and revising Life.Church contracts, including identifying and recommending additions or revisions to legal terms and analyzing risk exposure based on data privacy, legal terminology, confidentiality, and other risk factors. This role manages trademark registrations and renewals and facilitates corporate registrations. The Coordinator will identify and escalate contracts and other legal concerns to the Legal team appropriately. This role will also support office operations by managing the team budget and Legal inbox, responding to basic questions and inquiries and escalating to other Legal team members where appropriate. The Coordinator will also act as the main point of contact for the Conga system and support back-end management of the system.
This role is responsible for providing operational and administrative support in coordination with their team’s efforts to further Life.Church’s mission and reach people for Christ.

What You'll Do

Support Contract Creation and Review Processes
  • Manage Conga contracts system, reviewing and sorting contracts queue and approving contract terms.
  • Review all contracts submitted by Life.Church employees, analyzing potential points of liability, indemnity obligations, and other business terms in each contract under supervision of an attorney.
  • Provide analysis of contracts to leadership and obtain necessary approval of contract terms.
  • Suggest revisions on contracts to protect Life.Church from liability and provide favorable business terms.
  • Draft contracts using Life.Church’s standard legal terms when a contract is not provided.
  • Analyze global Bible contracts for YouVersion, collaborating with team during negotiations.
  • Ensure each contract is properly attributed in the Conga contracts system, supporting long-term storage initiatives.
  • Manage contract templates.
Support Legal Team Daily Operations
  • Manage certificates of insurability, ensuring they are obtained and up-to-date.
  • Correspond and communicate with contract owners regarding status of a contract and key points needing review.
  • Support back-end management of Conga contracts system (resetting passwords, training new users, etc.).
  • Train and provide learning materials regarding the contract process and related policies.
  • Manage the Legal team inbox, responding to questions or assigning tasks or projects as needed.
  • Triage questions from attendees or other churches regarding legal issues or materials, coordinating with Life.Church teams to provide guidance.
  • Manage the budgeting process for the Legal team, as needed.

  • Effective at multi-tasking, time management, and follow up to meet committed timelines.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills to foster relationships and partnerships.
  • Ability to self-motivate, take initiative, make independent decisions, and problem-solve.
  • Maintain a systematic and organized approach to completing assignments accurately, thoroughly, and timely.
  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Bachelor’s degree or Paralegal certification preferred.
  • 1-3 years of related work experience preferred.

Benefits We Offer

  • Paid parental leave, including maternity, paternity, and adoption leave.
  • Generous employer-paid leave for the use of vacation, sick time, and other qualifying reasons.
  • Innovative and comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance that provides team members with useful resources and savings to navigate their holistic health.
  • Life insurance policy provided for all staff members at 2x annual salary at no cost. Additional life insurance coverage is available to purchase.
  • Short-Term and Long-Term disability is covered at 100% for full-time qualified staff members.
  • Comprehensive wellness and mental health benefits allow staff to proactively invest in their physical and emotional health.
  • Generous 401(k) retirement plan allowing a team member to have up to 12.5% (including employee contribution, employer match, and employer discretionary contribution) contributed into their account in their first year. It doesn’t stop there—the more years on staff, the greater the investment!
  • $160 annually in development dollars for team members to invest in their professional growth.
  • Casual dress and work environment.
  • And much more!

Our Beliefs, Culture, and Commitment to Diversity

At Life.Church, every staff member, and intern is a minister and is expected to engage in the church's ministry fully. We consider ministry readiness and an individual’s capacity to represent Life.Church’s beliefs as a minister during the selection process for all staff and intern positions. An essential function within every position held by a staff member or intern at Life.Church is to uphold and represent the beliefs of Life.Church. Learn more about what we believe at Life.Church.
While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team through diversity. We know that diverse perspectives in race, ethnicity, background, age, and gender are essential to reaching the world for Christ. To learn more about how we strengthen our team through diversity, visit our careers page.

title: Document Controller
description:
Nous recherchons un(e) contrôleur(euse) documentaire expérimenté pour se joindre à l'équipe à Montréal, QC. L'incumbent sera responsable du traitement de la documentation interne et externe tout en maintenant l'utilisation des multiples systèmes et processus de gestion documentaire de l'organisation, et en veillant à ce que les processus de contrôle documentaire de Sedgman soient respectés.

We are seeking an experienced Document Controller to join the team in Montreal, QC. . The incumbent will be responsible for processing internal and external documentation while maintaining the use of the organization’s multiple document management systems and processes, and ensuring Sedgman’s document control processes are followed.

En quoi consiste ce poste? Responsabilités clés :

  • Gérer tous les documents du projet; maintenir le registre de contrôle des documents liés au projet.

  • Planifier, superviser et enregistrer le flux de documents vers/depuis les clients, les sous-traitants et les bureaux de projet.

  • Coordonner la documentation des fournisseurs, le contrôle des dessins, les transmissions et les tâches administratives générales.

  • Assurez-vous que les dessins sont enregistrés avec les révisions et détails appropriés et délivrés dans le délai demandé.

  • Émettre la documentation du projet aux parties prenantes internes et externes.

  • Fournir un soutien au contrôle documentaire aux équipes d'ingénierie au Canada, en Australie et à l'international.

What does this role involve ? Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage all project documents; maintaining project-related document control register.

  • Plan, supervise, and record document flow to/from clients, subcontractors, and project offices.

  • Coordinate vendor documentation, drawing control, transmittals, and general administrative tasks.

  • Ensure drawings are registered with correct revision & details and issued within the requested time frame.

  • Issue project documentation to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Provide document control support to engineering teams in Canada, Australia, and internationally.

Que recherchons-nous chez notre futur membre d'équipe? Qualifications :

  • Minimum de 5 à 8 ans d'expérience en contrôle de documents dans un bureau de projet d'ingénierie.

  • Expérience préalable en exigences de contrôle documentaire.

  • Capacité démontrée à construire et maintenir des flux de travail et l'automatisation autour du processus de contrôle documentaire.

  • Solides compétences en données fournisseurs et contrôle de révision.

  • Maîtrise de MS Office

  • L'expérience avec InEight – Les logiciels de documents sont essentielles.

  • Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles, attention aux détails et capacité à faire plusieurs choses à la fois.

  • Proactif dans l'enquête et la correction des écarts de contrôle documentaire

  • À l'aise de travailler dans un environnement rapide avec une pression constante sur les échéances.

  • À l'aise de travailler seul ainsi que de faire partie d'une équipe

  • Excellente maîtrise du français parlé et écrit. Une bonne maîtrise de l'anglais parlé est requise en raison des contacts quotidiens avec des clients, fournisseurs, partenaires et collègues basés hors du Québec.

  • Doit être autorisé à travailler au Canada sans parrainage.

What are we looking for in our future team member ? Qualifications:

  • Minimum 5 to 8 years’ experience in document control, within an engineering project office.

  • Previous experience in document control requirements.

  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain workflows and automation around the document control process.

  • Strong skills in vendor data and revision control.

  • Proficiency in MS Office

  • Experience with InEight is essential.

  • Experience in TeamBinder is beneficial

  • Excellent interpersonal skills, attention to detail, and ability to multitask.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with constant deadline pressure.

  • Comfortable working alone as well as part of a team

  • Language requirements: excellent spoken and written French. Strong spoken English skills are required due to daily contact with clients, suppliers, partners, and colleagues based outside Quebec.

  • Must be eligible to work in Canada without sponsorship

Qu'est-ce que vous y gagnez?

  • Régime de rémunération attractif : incluant un programme d'incitatifs à court terme (primes); une contrepartie REER, ainsi qu'un régime santé et avantages sociaux

  • Un portefeuille de travail passionnant et diversifié

  • Un fort accent sur l'apprentissage et le développement

  • Occasion de travailler sur des projets importants pour l'industrie minière canadienne

  • Potentiel significatif d'évolution de carrière

  • Accès à des mentors de renommée mondiale dans toutes les disciplines et produits

Sedgman Novopro Projects Inc., faisant partie du groupe CIMIC, est un fournisseur de premier plan de solutions de traitement et d'infrastructure minérale pour l'industrie mondiale des ressources. Axé sur l'industrie minière nord-américaine, Sedgman offre des services complets au cycle de vie des projets — du développement et l'exécution aux opérations en cours.

What is in it for you?

  • Attractive remuneration package : including Short term incentives (bonus) program; RRSP matching, and a Health and benefits package

  • Exciting and diverse pipeline of work

  • Strong focus on learning and development

  • Opportunity to work on significant projects for the Canadian mining industry

  • Significant career growth potential

  • Access to world leading mentors across disciplines and commodities

Sedgman Canada Limited, part of the CIMIC Group, is a leading provider of mineral processing and infrastructure solutions to the global resources industry. Focused on the North American mining industry, Sedgman delivers full project life cycle services—from development and execution to ongoing operations

title: Project Manager
description:
SUMMARY

The Project Manager plans and oversees the end-to-end delivery of assigned projects and ensures delivery within scope, budget and requirements.

At this position level:

  • Projects are typically of moderate complexity, risk and exposure.

KEY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

For the assigned projects:

  • Plans and oversees the end-to-end delivery of assigned projects. At this level, projects managed are typically of moderate complexity, risk and exposure.
  • In collaboration with project concerned parties, defines project scope, deliverables and requirements.
  • Develops and implements project plans.
  • Determines resource and budget requirements, cost estimates, and timelines.
  • Identifies project risks and develops and implements mitigation and contingency plans.
  • Monitors project delivery against timelines and ensures timely completion.
  • Oversees the activities of project team members and monitors project task completion.
  • Communicates project status to relevant concerned parties.
  • Ensures projects are delivered on time, within scope, budget and requirements, and complies with all regulatory, environmental and health and safety requirements.

Client Relationship Management

  • Develops and maintains effective relationships with clients.
  • Responsible for resolving issues, managing client expectations, and ensuring client satisfaction.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Urgent Project Requirements

  • Project will be initiated immediately; Project manager works with the operations team to identify and collect requirements.
  • Start an immediate risk assessment, cost estimates, and kick off meeting with all concerned parties as an introduction and forecast of next steps.
  • Funding is generally completed “on the fly” a good understanding of benchmarking, and or current industry costs to provide budgets to the client.
  • Able to work independently on challenges to ensure the project keeps moving.
  • Understands the importance of a regular cadence of communication.
  • Navigate the client’s organization, to capture who should be engaged and when for project updates.
  • Schedule updates, risks, and opportunity updates.

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS

  • Community college diploma in architectural technology, construction technology, engineering technology; required.
  • University degree in Architecture or Engineering, preferred.
  • 3 to 5 years of project management work experience.
  • Project management – proven ability and experience in delivering projects on-time, on-budget, within specifications and in-compliant with all requirements including but not limited to regulatory, environmental, health, and safety requirements.
  • Project Budget management – proven ability and experience in developing and managing budgets.
  • Project risk mitigation and management – proven ability and experience in mitigating and managing project risks.
  • Communication – strong communication, influence, persuasion, and negotiation skills.
  • Relationship building – proven ability and experience in building and maintaining effective relationships.
  • Client management – proven ability and experience in managing client relationships and expectations.
  • Client service orientation – strong client service orientation.
  • Project team leadership – proven ability and experience in project team leadership.
  • Vendor management – proven ability and experience in managing vendor performance.
  • Quality – possesses a continuous improvement and quality mindset along with a desire to continuously seek and incorporate best practices and technologies in order to optimize program delivery and deliver value to the client.
  • Computer proficiency – proficient in and experience with MS Office suite of applications along with proven ability to quickly learn new applications.
  • High sense of urgency.
  • Excellent communicator both verbal and written.
  • Able to create project schedules independently.
  • Ability to create class D estimates, without consultant support.
  • Strong multitasker, juggling multiple projects simultaneously at various stages of development.
  • Understanding of the construction industry.
  • Able to differentiate on reporting to executives and team members.
  • Create business cases for funding, with clear and precise information to ensure funding approvals.
  • Goal orientated.
  • Understanding of impacts and implements creative solutions.

Licenses and/or Professional Accreditation

One or more of the following would be considered an asset:

  • Project Management Institute Accreditation or in progress.
  • LEED certification or in progress.
  • Engineer in training.

This is a regular, full-time position with a salary range of $77,259 - $96,573 per annum. The starting salary will be based on the successful candidate’s competencies, including but not limited to experience, education and performance related to this role.

title: Director of Culinary Operations & Experiences - Aspen Hospitality
description:
Position Summary
The Director of Culinary Operations & Experiences defines and advances the culinary vision and standards across Aspen Hospitality’s portfolio of luxury and lifestyle hotels, resorts, restaurants, and private clubs. This role leads and develops Executive Chefs and culinary leaders across the portfolio, establishing shared standards, strengthening talent, and implementing effective systems while preserving each property's distinct identity. The Director is accountable for culinary excellence, exceptional guest and member experiences, and the financial performance of all food and beverage outlets. This position reports to the Vice President of Operations.

The salary range for this position is $185,000 - $212,000. Actual pay will be dependent on budget and experience; all our salaried roles are eligible for bonus.

Job Posting Deadline
Applications for this position will be accepted until October 25, 2026.

Essential Job Functions/Key Job Responsibilities
• Define the culinary philosophy for the portfolio and lead menu strategies across all outlets, balancing creativity, seasonality, local sourcing, and profitability while preserving each property's distinct identity
• Develop, refresh, and reposition restaurant and bar concepts in partnership with property leadership
• Establish brand culinary standards, recipe specifications, and plating guidelines for each concept, and lead awards and ratings readiness, including Forbes Travel Guide, Michelin, and AAA standards where applicable
• Conduct regular property visits and audits to ensure consistency and execution of culinary standards
• Oversee food safety, sanitation, and allergen programs, ensuring full regulatory compliance in every jurisdiction
• Manage food cost, labor productivity, and kitchen operating budgets across the portfolio, and partner with finance and property leaders on food and beverage forecasting, pricing, and P&L reviews
• Direct menu engineering and purchasing strategy to grow margins without compromising quality, and identify revenue opportunities in private dining, events, catering, and club programs
• Build and manage relationships with farmers, ranchers, purveyors, and specialty suppliers, and lead portfolio-level negotiations to secure favorable pricing and consistent supply, including in remote mountain markets
• Advance sustainability and responsible sourcing practices across the portfolio
• Lead, coach, and develop Executive Chefs and culinary leaders at every property, fostering a respectful, collaborative kitchen culture aligned with company values
• Partner with Human Resources on recruiting, succession planning, and retention, including seasonal staffing and housing challenges, and building training programs and career pathways to attract and retain culinary talent
• Lead culinary planning for new openings, outlet renovations, and concept launches, including kitchen design, equipment specification, capital expenditure priorities, and delivery of opening menus, teams, and systems on time and on budget
• Other duties as assigned

Education & Experience Requirements
• Culinary degree or equivalent classical culinary training preferred
• Current food safety management certification, such as ServSafe Manager, or the ability to obtain certification, required
• Minimum of 7 years of progressive culinary leadership, including at least 3 years in people leadership and multi-property initiatives, required

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
• Executive Chef leadership in a luxury hotel or resort environment
• Leadership in multi-unit, regional, or corporate culinary operations overseeing multiple properties or concepts
• A proven record of success in five-star or five-diamond environments or nationally recognized restaurants
• Demonstrated P&L ownership with measurable results in food cost, labor management, and revenue growth
• Successful leadership of at least one hotel or restaurant pre-opening
• Strong knowledge of banquet and catering operations in high-volume luxury settings
• Willingness and ability to travel frequently across the portfolio, including mountain resort markets with seasonal peaks
• Knowledge of resort and seasonal markets, including mountain destinations
• Familiarity with private club dining and member-focused programming
• Recognition through culinary awards, media coverage, or industry leadership
• Proficiency with kitchen management, inventory, and procurement systems
• Ability to balance creative culinary vision with the operational discipline required to deliver consistent results across every service
• Ability to develop talent and lead Executive Chefs through coaching and clear standards, while modeling respect, inclusion, and accountability
• Strong commercial acumen, with a focus on aligning culinary quality, guest and member satisfaction, and financial performance
• Ability to collaborate effectively with General Managers, food and beverage leaders, marketing, and finance

Work Environment & Physical Demands
• Ability to reach, crouch, kneel, stand, walk or be on your feet for extended periods of time
• Regularly work in wet, hot and humid conditions for extended periods of time and may be required to walk on slippery and uneven surfaces
• Must be able to occasionally lift, push or pull up to 50 lbs. individually or with assistance (weight limits can vary according to position, but no more than 50)

Job Benefits
This position is classified as a regular full-time position eligible for the following benefits:
Enrollment dates differ across the various programs.
• Health, Dental and Vision Insurance Programs
• Flexible Spending Account Programs
• Life Insurance Programs
• Paid Time Off Programs
• Paid Leave Programs
• 401(k) Savings Plan
• Employee Ski Pass and Dependent Ski Passes
• Other company perks

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. By accepting a position with Aspen One, Aspen Snowmass, Aspen Ventures or Aspen Hospitality you acknowledge that you are able to perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. To request accommodation during the application and interviewing process, please contact Human Resources at 970-300-7700.

This job description is designed to indicate the general nature and level of work. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive list of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. Duties and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

Aspen One is an equal opportunity employer (Minority/Female/Disabled/Veteran). At Aspen One, inclusion, equity, and diversity are fundamental to fulfilling our vision of building a better workplace and better world. From our hiring practices through the entire employee experience, we embrace and celebrate the unique experiences, perspectives and cultural backgrounds that each employee brings to the workplace. We encourage diverse points of view which allows us to develop innovative solutions to the ever-evolving world of work. Aspen One strives to foster an environment where our employees feel respected, valued and empowered, and our team members are at the forefront of helping us promote and sustain an inclusive workplace that works for all.

title: Head of Compute
description:
Who We Are

Hyperbolic Labs is on a mission to democratize AI by breaking down the barriers to computing power with our Open-Access AI Cloud. By making better use of idle computing resources across the globe, we offer an innovative GPU marketplace and AI inference service that promise affordability and accessibility for all. As pioneers at the intersection of AI and open-source technology, we believe in an open future where AI innovation is limited only by imagination, not by access to resources. We're looking for forward-thinking individuals who share our passion for making AI universally accessible, secure, and affordable. Join us in building a platform that empowers innovators everywhere to turn their visionary AI projects into reality.

About the Role

We're seeking a Head of Compute to build and scale the GPU supply side of Hyperbolic's marketplace. This is a relationships-first role where your existing connections with data centers, NeoClouds, and GPU suppliers are your most valuable asset. You'll be responsible for onboarding a large number of NeoCloud providers to our platform, sourcing GPU capacity through your network, and ensuring we always have the supply needed to meet customer demand. This isn't a traditional supply chain role—we're looking for someone who knows the GPU landscape intimately, has direct relationships with suppliers, and can pick up the phone to find capacity when needed.

You will manage ongoing supplier relationships, maintain accurate inventory and pricing data, process reserve deals by matching customer requests with the right suppliers, and work closely with our sales team to rapidly respond to "Can you find me X GPUs?" requests. You'll ensure our scaling limit is demand, not supply availability. This role combines supplier relationship management, deal sourcing, and technical understanding of GPU infrastructure—requiring someone who can talk technical details with engineers while building deep partnerships with data center operators.

Who You Are

  • Established relationships with data centers, NeoClouds, and GPU suppliers with a proven track record of sourcing GPU capacity directly

  • Deep knowledge of the GPU landscape including where capacity exists, key players in the market, and how to access underutilized resources

  • Experience sourcing from multiple NeoClouds or data centers, or similar GPU aggregators

  • Technical background or strong technical understanding that enables engineer-to-engineer conversations about infrastructure and GPU specifications

  • Proven ability to build and maintain supplier relationships, onboard new partners, and manage ongoing account dynamics

  • Strong deal-making and negotiation skills with ability to match customer needs with supplier capabilities

  • Excellent organizational skills to manage inventory data, pricing information, and supplier engagement across 70-100+ providers

  • Ability to move quickly and respond to urgent capacity requests from sales and customers

  • Strong communication skills for coordinating between suppliers, internal teams, and customers

  • Demonstrated stability in previous roles with commitment to building long-term relationships and infrastructure

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience at GPU aggregators, cloud marketplaces, or companies managing multi-supplier GPU networks

  • Existing relationships with major NeoCloudsKnowledge of bare metal data center operations and capacity planning

  • Understanding of GPU types, specifications, and use cases for AI/ML workloads

  • Experience with supplier onboarding processes, inventory management systems, and pricing dynamics

  • Track record of scaling supplier networks from tens to hundreds of partners

  • Background in high-growth startups or marketplaces where supply availability was a key constraint

Hyperbolic is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Salesforce Project Manager
description:
About Us - CloudMasonry

CloudMasonry is a full-service Salesforce consultancy with multi-cloud expertise, serving enterprise clients through onshore, collaborative teams. Senior consultants shape the solution, and we were the first Salesforce consultancy to build AI into a complete delivery methodology, where it keeps requirements, documentation, and reporting moving so our teams spend more time with clients.
With offices in the US and UK, 65+ consultants holding 350+ Salesforce certifications, 559+ completed projects, a 4.9 CSAT, and an 89% repeat-client rate, CloudMasonry works with enterprise clients on their most complex Salesforce programs.

About the Role

The Project Manager is responsible for coordinating and delivering projects from start to finish, ensuring all objectives are met on time and within budget. This role oversees every aspect of project execution, setting deadlines, assigning responsibilities, and tracking progress, while providing regular status reports to senior leadership and client executives. The Project Manager proactively identifies and escalates risks or issues, manages budgets and financials, and leverages experience and sound judgment to develop plans and achieve goals. This position leads and directs the work of others, fostering a collaborative environment that allows for creativity, autonomy, and effective problem-solving. This is a fully remote opportunity open to candidates located within the United States. This role includes moderate travel (typically around 25%, with occasional increases based on project needs) and requires a high degree of self-management.

Key Responsibilities

  • Works effectively both independently and in collaboration with CloudMasonry and customer team members to drive customer satisfaction and success.

  • Oversees and takes full accountability for the successful completion of all aspects of assigned project work.

  • Exercises independent judgment and can lead enterprise-level projects with minimal oversight from a director or engagement manager.

  • Facilitates meetings effectively, demonstrates strong brainstorming and consensus-building skills, and confidently engages with executive-level project sponsors.

  • Frequently called upon to take a leadership role in CloudMasonry sales initiatives within areas of expertise.

  • Drives project delivery by managing cross-functional teams, removing blockers, and enforcing best practices across Agile, hybrid, or traditional delivery models.

  • Develops and maintains project plans, timelines, and resource allocations, ensuring delivery commitments are met and client expectations are effectively managed.

  • Owns risk identification and mitigation planning, escalating critical issues with well-defined recommendations and impact assessments.

  • Manages project financials, including budgeting, forecasting, and monitoring project burn rate to ensure alignment with scope. Proactively communicates budget status and risks to internal and client stakeholders.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Documentation & Tools Expertise:
Demonstrates the ability to effectively prepare and maintain key project documentation, including:

  • Business Process Documentation

  • Process Flow Analysis

  • Requirements Definition

  • Configuration Workbooks

  • Data Models

  • Detailed Functional Designs

  • Executive Summaries

  • Project Plans

  • Strong experience with project management tools and methodologies, including RAID Logs and RACI Matrices

Certifications (Preferred):

  • Salesforce Administrator Certification

  • Salesforce Sales Cloud or Service Cloud Certification

Leadership Skills:

  • Sets deadlines for project team members and ensures accountability

  • Lead and mentor a team of 2–4 delivery resources, driving project execution, maintaining quality standards, and fostering professional growth

  • Monitors progress and conducts regular follow-ups

  • Offers constructive and respectful feedback

  • Escalates issues appropriately when necessary

  • Identifies areas of risk and develops mitigation plans

  • Proactively seeks opportunities for professional growth

  • Commits to earning one technical certification per quarter, as directed by their manager or supervisor

  • Willingness to travel with clients or project teams as needed

Required Skills & Experience:

  • 2–5 years of hands-on experience managing Salesforce projects

  • Technical background or relevant degree program preferred

  • Experience with or Vlocity

  • Strong oral and written communication skills

  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities

  • Travel requirements are contingent on client needs and may range from approximately 25% to 50%

  • Ability to articulate the benefits of the Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) model

  • Deep knowledge of enterprise system implementation and configuration, including Salesforce, SFA, or ERP systems

  • Quick learner with strong creative problem-solving skills

  • Strong team player with leadership potential and interpersonal strengths

  • Detail-oriented, with the ability to quickly absorb and apply new concepts, business models, and technologies

Benefits & Perks

  • Full-time position with a competitive salary

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • 401(k) plan with 50% employer match up to 4%

  • Unlimited PTO to maintain work-life balance

  • Parental leave for new parents

  • Paid company holidays

  • Salesforce certification reimbursement

  • Performance-based bonus eligibility

Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion

At CloudMasonry, diverse perspectives drive innovation. We embrace candidates from all backgrounds and experiences to build a stronger, more inclusive team. You will find your place with us if you are passionate about problem-solving and collaboration.

Application Process

After submitting your resume, you will receive an email invitation to complete an applicant assessment. This assessment helps us align your skills and attributes with the role. Candidates who do not complete the assessment will not be considered for the position.

Join CloudMasonry and take your Salesforce consulting career to the next level!

We participate in E-Verify, a federal program used to confirm employment eligibility and authorization to work in the United States.

title: Sr. Specialist – L2 Body Integration
description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

At Scout Motors, you don't just design vehicles- you shape the future of the road. Our Engineering team is where bold ideas meet rigorous execution, building machines that are as durable and capable as the people who drive them. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with brilliant minds across disciplines, turning complex challenges into elegant, scalable solutions that meet the highest standards of safety, performance, and user experience. This is a place where your fingerprints are found on metal – where what you design gets built, driven, and remembered. If you're hungry to engineer something that matters, Scout Motors is where that ambition finds its highest gear.

We are seeking a talented Senior Engineer – Body Features Integration & Validation to support the development, integration, and validation of advanced body features for next-generation Software Defined Vehicle (SDV) platforms. This role focuses on vehicle body electronics and customer-facing body features including closures, lighting, access systems, occupant controls, smart actuators, comfort systems, and connected body functions. The engineer will drive feature integration and validation activities across HIL (Hardware-in-the-Loop), SIL (Software-in-the-Loop), bench, and vehicle environments. The ideal candidate has strong experience in body control systems, ECU integration, diagnostics, vehicle networking, and SDV architectures with a passion for delivering robust customer-facing vehicle experiences.

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

  • Own integration of all domain controllers and distributed ECUs into the vehicle E/E architecture with focus in Body systems.
  • Own Software Integration & Validation per vehicle software maturity, performance and release gates and approve vehicle integration builds (per milestones).
  • Integrate and validate vehicle body features across prototype, bench, HIL, SIL, and vehicle test environments.
  • Support feature integration for smart access systems, power doors and liftgates, interior and exterior lighting, window and sunroof controls, seat and occupant comfort systems, Body Control Module (BCM) features, passive entry/passive start systems
  • Coordinate software and hardware compatibility across body ECUs, gateways, and zonal controllers.
  • Support features bring-up, calibration validation, and vehicle-level functionality testing.
  • Validation responsible for network topology, gateway routing strategies, signal database integrity (DBC, ARXML), bandwidth utilization and bus loading
  • Validate and manage vehicle communication across CAN / CAN-FD, LIN, Automotive Ethernet (100/1000BASE-T1), FlexRay network framework
  • Validate and release bootloader compatibility, flashing strategy, partitioning strategy (AUTOSAR Classic/Adaptive), Memory and CPU utilization budgets
  • Develop and execute HIL and SIL test cases for body feature functionality and subsystem interactions.
  • Validate feature behaviors, diagnostics, fault handling, and software integration using simulation environments.
  • Validate wake-up/sleep strategies across ECUs, ensure no unintended current draw or parasitic drain and correct power state transitions during vehicle power cycles, start/stop/sleep, OTA updates/events
  • Validate UDS/DoIP response timing, diagnostic sessions do not degrade functional performance, DTC accuracy and freeze frame integrity and robustness.

Location & Travel Expectations:

  • This role may be based out of the Scout Motors corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC.
  • This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.
  • Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

  • Master’s degree in electrical engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with 10+ yrs. of experience
  • Strong understanding of vehicle E/E architecture and ECU-level software stacks, automotive communication protocols (CAN, LIN, FlexRay, Ethernet), UDS diagnostics (ISO 14229) and diagnostic communication tools
  • Expert knowledge of Jira, GitHub/GitLab, Jenkins, and Artifactory.ALM/PLMProficiency in Siemens Polarion, IBM DOORS Next Gen, or PTC Windchill.
  • Strong understanding, development and verification of plant and control models in MATLAB/Simulink for execution in hardware in the loop test environment, dSpace control desk and automation desk
  • Strong understanding of 1st principles in Engineering, result/solution oriented.
  • Familiarity with SW for embedded systems, EE systems and architecture
  • Familiarity with A2B, CAN, Automotive Ethernet, LIN, LVDS communication protocols and Vehicle Network tools, such as CANalyzer, CANoe, etc.‚
  • Expertise with complex problem solving, data analysis, access/interpret/drive results with extended teams.
  • Knowledge of Automotive design and development process, system requirements, and general engineering best practices

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up. This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation. In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

  • Competitive insurance including:
    • Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans
  • 401(k) program with:
    • An employer match and immediate vesting
  • Generous Paid Time Off including:
    • 20 days planned PTO, as accrued
    • 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually
    • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders
    • Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $140,000.00 - $170,000.00
